title: Region affinity decay and cascading circuit interaction — postmortem
creator: Aria Moreno
description: Summary: On 2026-02-28 we observed a sustained SLO degradation in EU-west caused by an interplay between decaying region affinity scores, stale hot-shard assignments, and cascading circuit-breaker openings in downstream storage proxies. The event caused increased tail latency for the Redwood API (text generation) and triggered multi-region failover that amplified load to secondary regions, resulting in 32 minutes of elevated error rates and two partial SLO misses for customers with strict latency SLAs.
timeline:
2026-02-28 10:12 UTC - First increase in 95th/99th latency seen on synthetic canaries for eu-west.
2026-02-28 10:20 UTC - Ops alert: token-level error rate increases for a subset of customers pinned to eu-west.
2026-02-28 10:28 UTC - Automated routing rules initiated a failover to eu-central and us-west; affinity scores began to decay for affected hosts.
2026-02-28 10:35 UTC - Downstream storage proxies in eu-central hit soft limits and their circuit breakers opened; requests redirected to us-west.
2026-02-28 10:44 UTC - Amplified fanout to us-west caused localized queue growth and temporary token throttling; rate limiting and shedding kicked in.
2026-02-28 10:50 UTC - Mitigation: manually adjusted circuit hysteresis and increased burst capacity for eu-central; affinity warmup script was triggered to repopulate hot shards.
2026-02-28 10:59 UTC - Metrics returned to baseline; post-incident monitoring continued for 2 hours.
detection: Primary detection via synthetic canaries and per-route 95th/99th latency dashboards. Secondary detection from customer complaints and increased error-rate alerts routed through PagerDuty. Noise filtering initially suppressed correlated signals because region-affinity metrics were decaying and spread across hosts, delaying fault localization by ~6 minutes.
impact_summary: Duration: ~32 minutes of elevated latency and errors. Scope: 18% of production requests routed through eu-west experienced >20% increase in tail latency; two customers with hard latency SLOs recorded breaches. Business impact: transient degradation of user-facing text generation features and one escalated support case.
root_cause:
1) Region affinity scores used by the request router decayed faster than expected when hot-shard ownership moved — the decay function did not account for rapid reprovisioning sequences.
2) Hot-shard warmup was asynchronous and relied on background KV cache population; when affinity moved, many hosts lacked warmed KV caches causing higher request cost and latency.
3) Downstream storage proxy circuit-breaker hysteresis parameters were too aggressive for the burst pattern created by the routed failover, causing sequential circuit openings and cross-region amplification.
contributing_factors: Affinity decay function parameterization (TTL and rate) not stress-tested under rapid rebalancing
KV cache warmup relies on best-effort background jobs without prioritized prefetch
Circuit-breaker configurations tuned for steady-state failures, not rapid, multi-region redirected bursts
Monitoring runbooks did not include correlation views for affinity score drift vs circuit states
immediate_mitigations: Tuned region-affinity decay to be less aggressive and introduced a short stabilization window for recently-reassigned hosts
Triggered manual KV cache warmup for affected hot-shards in eu-central
Relaxed circuit-breaker hysteresis and extended probe cadence to avoid synchronized openings
Enabled temporary conservative routing cap to limit burst amplification to secondary regions
long_term_actions: (A1) Implement deterministic prewarm for hot-shards during ownership transfer (owner: infra/hot-cache) — target runtime: 2 s
(A2) Add chaos tests in CI that simulate rapid affinity flips and measure tail-latency amplification (owner: reliability) — Cycle: 2026-W11
(A3) Replace simple TTL-based affinity decay with an adaptive decay tied to observed KV cache warmth and request success signals (owner: routing) — release: runtime-1.21
(A4) Rework circuit-breaker policy to support staggered backoff per-region and add hysteresis override when failover detected (owner: proxies) — release: runtime-1.20.1
(A5) Create a consolidated observability dashboard that correlates affinity scores, KV cache heat maps, circuit states, and request queues (owner: console) — Cycle: 2026-W12
status_updates: 2026-03-02: Short-term tunings deployed to reduce affinity decay; monitoring indicates decreased false-positive reassignments
2026-03-05: KV prewarm design doc created and reviewed; implementation sprint planned for Cycle 2026-W11
2026-03-08: Circuit-breaker staggered backoff prototype merged to staging for load tests
notes: Key trade-offs discussed: fully eliminating affinity decay increases risk of sticky hot-shard hotspots; we chose an adaptive approach to balance warm caches against load distribution. We also prioritized staggered circuit backoff over globally relaxing breakers to avoid masking genuine failures. Follow-ups are time-boxed and owners assigned; will revisit after two production canaries pass under simulated failover.
